title: unified rollouts: add observability hooks and safety guards for canary + auto-rollback
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: production rollouts (canary, A/B, shadow) are a key piece of Redwood's model lifecycle, but we lacked consistent observability and a small but critical set of safety guards for automated rollback paths. This PR introduces metric and trace hooks at every rollout phase, improves rollback decision transparency, and adds safety toggles to prevent noisy or system-wide incidents from triggering harmful automated rollbacks. Summary of changes: 1) Observability: emit rollout lifecycle metrics (rollout.start, rollout.progress, rollout.complete, rollout.rollback) with tags (env, model, rollout_strategy, stage, region, route). Add tracing spans for canary probe evaluation and rollback decisions (linkable to request traces). Wire metrics into the Console's Rollout Inspector view and add server-side debug logging for decision inputs. 2) Safety guards: add global "rollback_suppression_window" that prevents auto-rollback when cluster-level incidents or existing high-error-rate windows are detected; configurable per-tenant. Add conservative default thresholds (error-rate >= 2.5% sustained over 3m, latency-p90 regression >= 50% over baseline) and a grace period before auto-rollback triggers. Implement a manual kill-switch (feature flag + RBAC check) to disable auto-rollback for a tenant. 3) Decision transparency: persist rollout evaluation history and top contributing signals to the rollout object for quick post-mortems; expose in API and Console. 4) Tests & docs: add e2e tests for staged shadow/canary patterns and new safety scenarios; update unified-rollouts observability documentation and migration notes. Checklist: - [x] Add metrics/tracing hooks - [x] Implement suppression window + kill-switch - [x] Expose evaluation history in API - [x] Console UI updates (Rollout Inspector) - [x] Add e2e tests and stability guards - [x] Update docs & release notes Backwards compatibility & migration: new safety guards default to conservative opt-in behavior for tenants on Dedicated/Private; hosted customers will see conservative default thresholds applied automatically but can opt out via Console. No breaking API changes; rollout objects have optional new fields (evaluation_history, safety_state) which are absent for older rollouts. Testing: unit tests added for policy logic, integration tests validate suppression window behavior, e2e suite covers end-to-end canary -> auto-rollback scenario and manual override. Rolling changes: feature flagged and enabled for internal canary before org-wide rollout. Related: ENG-3124 (observability for rollouts), ENG-3189 (auto-rollback safety), SUP-4421 (customer incident that motivated suppression window).

review_comments: Ethan Park (review): Can we make the suppression window configurable per-tenant and also expose a read-only view in Console? Author: yes — added tenant-level config and Console read-only status in this PR.

Sofia Martinez (review): Unit tests for throttling logic flaked locally; please add a deterministic clock mock. Author: addressed — policy tests now use deterministic clock and CI showed stability after rerun.

Rajesh Nair (review): Would prefer default thresholds to be more conservative (2.5% -> 3%). Author: kept 2.5% based on incident post-mortem, but switched to tenant-overridable and documented rationale in docs.

SRE (comment): how does this interact with cluster-wide incident alerting? Author: suppression window will consult cluster-incident API (graceful no-op if API returns error); added fallback documented.
Author (final): squashed and addressed all comments; added e2e test to cover manual kill-switch behavior.

release_notes: Added rollout observability (rollout.start/progress/complete/rollback metrics and tracing); introduced rollback suppression window and tenant-level kill-switch to prevent inappropriate auto-rollbacks; exposed rollout evaluation history in API and Console; conservative default thresholds for auto-rollback introduced; new e2e tests for rollout safety guards.
